formal_statement: For all sufficiently large natural k and every integer n with 2k<n and n<=exp((log k)^2/(16 log(log k))), there is a natural prime p with k<p<2k dividing Pprod k n.
proof_changes: Use r0=ceil(log k/(8 log(log k))) instead of denominator 10.
Replace the first large-range logarithmic decay exponent -19/14 by -38/35, which remains strictly below -1.
Separate the exceptional minimal exponent r=3 and retain its k^(-1/18) saving; keep the existing log^(-10/9) envelope for r>=4.
failed_checks_retained: The naive uniform reuse of log^(-10/9) for all r>=3 fails after changing 1/20 to 1/16; the r=3 branch must retain its power saving.
Lean error-recovery runs containing sorryAx exited nonzero and are not certificates.
scope_limits: The Lean proof treats Baker-Harman-Pintz as the named axiom bhp, exactly as upstream.
The certificate improves a lower-bound exponent constant; it does not determine the main term or close the upper-bound side of Erdős problem 451.
Kernel checking is exact formal evidence, but the same session authored the patch, so AMRA independent natural-language reconstruction is still pending.
